entries.core_move: Convert a continuous-time signal from $x(t)$ to $x(-t)$ by mapping every time location $t_0$ to $-t_0$ and recognizing reversal as negative time scaling in the time-domain operation sequence.
Reflect the graph of $x(t)$ across $t=0$ by moving each feature at time $t_0$ to $-t_0$ while preserving its amplitude.

Convert a continuous-time piecewise definition $x(t)$ into the correctly ordered interval definition for $x(-t)$ by reflecting each breakpoint across $t=0$ and substituting $-t$ into the segment formulas.
Convert an exponential signal $x(t)=Ae^{(\sigma+j\omega)t}$ into $x(-t)=Ae^{-(\sigma+j\omega)t}$ and interpret the result as reversing growth or decay and complex-rotation direction.
Map each original signal time point $t_0$ to $t=(t_0-b)/a$ for $x(at+b)$ to interpret the combined shift, scale, and possible reversal of a continuous-time signal.

entries.lesson_title: Order of Operations in Signal Transformations
entries.core_move: Sequence time shifts, time scaling, and time reversal correctly when converting between a continuous-time signal's transformed expression and its resulting graph.
